71527.subject: Biology
71527.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
71527.text: Which plant breeding technique was used to produce NP 836 variety of wheat (rust resistant), Indore-2 variety of cotton (resistant to boll worm), Regina-II variety of cabbage (resistant to bacterial rot), etc.?
71527.sol: NP 836 is a variety of wheat that is resistant to rust and was developed through mutation breeding using X-rays. Similarly, Indore-2 variety of cotton (resistant to bollworm) and Regina-II variety of cabbage (resistant to bacterial rot) were also developed using mutation breeding. Mutation breeding involves exposing seeds or plants to radiation (like X-rays or gamma rays) or chemicals to induce mutations, followed by selecting the plants with desirable traits. Answer: Mutation breeding.

71846.subject: Chemistry
71846.text: In the combustion reaction of alkanes, if 1 mole of ethane is burnt, find number of moles of oxygen required?
71846.sol: The general equation for the combustion of an alkane C_nH_ 2n+2 is given by: C_nH_ 2n+2 + ( 3n+1 2 ) O₂ n CO₂ + (n+1) H₂O For ethane ( C₂H₆ ), n = 2 . Substituting n = 2 in the coefficient of O₂ : Moles of O₂ required = 3(2)+1 2 = 7 2 = 3.5 The balanced chemical equation is: C₂H₆ + 3.5 O₂ 2 CO₂ + 3 H₂O Thus, 1 mole of ethane requires 3.5 moles of oxygen. Answer: 3.5

72127.subject: Physics
72127.text: A galvanometer can be converted into a voltmeter of certain range by connecting a resistance of 990 in series with it. When the resistance of 480 is connected in series, the range is halved. The resistance of the galvanometer is
72127.sol: Let the resistance of the galvanometer be G and the full-scale deflection current be I_g . When a resistance of 990 is connected in series, the range of the voltmeter is V . V = I_g (G + 990) When a resistance of 480 is connected in series, the range is halved, i.e., V 2 . V 2 = I_g (G + 480) Dividing the first equation by the second equation: V V 2 = I_g (G + 990) I_g (G + 480) 2 = G + 990 G + 480 2(G + 480) = G + 990 2G + 960 = G + 990 G = 30 Answer: 30

79959.sol: The amount of living matter present in an ecosystem in its different trophic levels is called standing crop. It is expressed in the form of number or biomass per unit area. 80103.subject: Botany
80103.text: Root hairs develop from the region of
80103.sol: The entire root is covered with the epidermis, a single layer of closely packed cells that often have thin projections known as root hairs. In roots, the root hairs arise from the zone of maturation. This is a differentiated zone bearing root hairs. The root tip contains the root apical meristem. Above the root tip, there is a multicellular root cap. Behind the root apical meristem, there is a zone of elongation.

Such vascular bundles because of the presence of cambium possess the ability to form secondary xylem and phloem tissues, and hence are called open vascular bundles. 123528.sol: Cell division is a very important process in all living organisms. During the division of a cell, DNA replication and cell growth also take place. 95307.sol: The environmental and physiological factors influence the cambium activity, due to which the climatic conditions in the temperate regions which are not uniform results in the cambium changes. In the spring season, the cambium activity increases to a great extent and a large number of xylary elements are produced, having vessels with wider cavities and the name given to this wood is the springwood or earlywood. 95536.sol: Members of this phylum are found in the Ocean and never been reported in freshwater resources like river stream etc.

95570.subject: Botany
95570.text: The members of which of the following phyla are exclusively marine?
95570.sol: Echinoderms are invertebrates with spiny skin, water vascular system and a simple nervous system. This phylum is majorly a marine group and found in all oceans. They are not found in freshwater or terrestrial surfaces. There are around 7000 species of this group which found exclusively in marine environments. The other three phyla habitat various ecologies such as freshwater, terrestrial environments and marine waters.

95666.subject: Botany
95666.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding Deuteromycetes? I . Deuteromycetes are called perfect fungi. I I . Members of Deuteromycetes were often moved to ascomycetes or basidiomycetes once their sexual stages were studied. I I I . Large number of Deuteromycetes are decomposers that help in nutrient cycling. I V . Their mycelium is aseptate and unbranched.
options: I , I I a n d I V
I I a n d I I I
I I I a n d I V
I , I I I a n d I V
95666.sol: Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi. The mode of sexual reproduction is not known in them. Once sexual stages of members of deuteromycetes were discovered they were often moved to ascomycetes and basidiomycetes. The members of deuteromycetes have septate and branched hyphae. Some members are saprophytes or parasites while a large number of them are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling. Some examples are Alternaria , Colletotrichum and Trichoderma .

95675.subject: Botany
95675.text: The incipient nucleus is present in
95675.sol: Cyanobacteria belong to myxophyceae and are also known as blue-green algae. They are photosynthetic organisms having chlorophyll similar to higher plants. Unlike other bacteria, they carry out oxygenic photosynthesis as they are capable of utilizing water as a source of hydrogen in photosynthesis. These cyanobacteria consist of an incipient nucleus, which is a nucleoid or primitive nucleus dispersed in the cytoplasm.

95678.subject: Botany
95678.text: Which of the following statement/s is/are not the characteristic feature of Kingdom Protista? ( a ) They include chrysophytes, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime molds, and protozoans ( b ) Chief producers in the ocean are diatoms. ( c ) Toxins are released by some of the members of this kingdom. ( d ) They are either unicellular or multicellular.
95678.sol: All single-celled eukaryotes are placed under Protista, but the boundaries of this kingdom are not well-defined. What may be 'a photosynthetic protistan' to one biologist may be 'a plant' to others. Chrysophytes, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime moulds and protozoans are included under Protista. Members of Protista are primarily aquatic. Diatoms are chief producers of the ocean, and dinoflagellates are known to release some toxic substances.

95941.subject: Botany
95941.text: The major drawback of the two-kingdom classification system was that it did not distinguish between
95941.sol: The Two Kingdom system of classification with Plantae and Animalia kingdoms was developed that included all plants and animals respectively. This system did not distinguish between the eukaryotes and prokaryotes, unicellular and multicellular organisms and photosynthetic (green algae) and non-photosynthetic (fungi) organisms. Classification of organisms into plants and animals was easily done and was easy to understand, but, a large number of organisms did not fall into either category. Hence the two kingdom classi

96376.text: Chiasmata are most clearly visualised in which stage?
96376.sol: The beginning of diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers. These X-shaped structures are called chiasmata that appear in diplotene stage.

96908.text: Select the correct match based on the type of aestivation of corolla and their examples.
96908.sol: Aestivation is the mode of arrangement of sepals or petals in floralbud with respect to the other members of the same whorl. There are four main types of aestivation, Valvate- Calotropis, Twisted - China rose, ladyfinger, cotton, Imbricate - Cassia and Gulmohar, Vexillary - Pea, Bean.

97433.subject: Botany
97433.text: Statement-I: The mesophyll of Pinus shows no distinction as spongy mesophyll and palisade. Statement-II: Parenchymatous cells are present in the mesophyll of Pinus .
97433.sol: Within the hypodermis of Pinus leaf is the parenchymatous mesophyll. It is comparted and shows no differentiation into palisade and spongy tissues. It consists of thin-walled cells which contain numerous chloroplasts and abundant starch. The mesophyll thus functions as the chlorophyll bearing tissue which manufactures food for plants.

97628.subject: Botany
97628.text: Which of the following reactions does not release CO 2 ?
97628.sol: In lactic acid fermentation, C O 2 is not released, as there is no step of decarboxylation unlike alcohol fermentation. The alcohol fermentation includes the decarboxylation of pyruvic acid to Acetaldehyde, which is further reduced to ethanol due to the reducing agent NADH (which gets oxidized to NAD + . Aerobic respiration (amphibolic pathway) releases CO 2 due to oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvic acid to Acetyl-CoA.

97646.subject: Botany

97646.sol: The pyruvate molecule enters the mitochondrial matrix where it is converted to acetyl-CoA by a reaction known as oxidative decarboxylation in presence of oxidizing agent NAD + . The enzyme responsible for this reaction is pyruvate dehydrogenase and the cofactor is Mg ++ .

Every coenzyme is a cofactor but every cofactor is not a coenzyme

98374.subject: Chemistry
98374.text: How many of the following statements are correct regarding properties of enzyme? (i) It lowers down the activation energy of the reaction. (ii) An active site of the enzyme is the pocket into which the substrate fits. (iii) The catalytic structure of most of the enzyme is globular and primary. (iv) Carbonic anhydrase enzyme is considered as the fastest enzyme.
98374.sol: Enzymes are made up of proteins that show the tertiary or quarternary structure and are generally globular proteins. This complex coiling and folding results in the formation of a cavity or pocket known as active site to which substrate binds forming ES complex. Enzyme catalyzes a reaction by lowering down the activation energy of the reaction. The carbonic anhydrase enzyme is one of the fastest enzymes with a typical catalytic rate ranges between 104 and 106 reactions per second.

306520.text: A closed bottle contains some liquid. As time progresses, the amount of the liquid stays constant. In the remaining space of the bottle, the vapour
306520.sol: Since the amount of liquid in the closed bottle remains constant as time progresses, the system has achieved a state of dynamic equilibrium. At this stage, the rate of evaporation of the liquid is exactly equal to the rate of condensation of the vapour. This equilibrium condition implies that the space above the liquid contains the maximum possible amount of vapour at the given temperature. Therefore, the vapour in the remaining space of the bottle must be saturated.
